title: Number of Arithmetic Triplets
statement: You get an integer array `nums` whose values strictly increase from left to right, and a positive integer `diff`. Count the index triples `(i, j, k)` with `i < j < k` such that `nums[j]` is exactly `diff` more than `nums[i]` and `nums[k]` is exactly `diff` more than `nums[j]`. Return how many such triples exist.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every triple works for 200 values but costs O(n³). Since `nums` strictly increases, a triple is fixed entirely by its last value `x`: the other two must be exactly `x - diff` and `x - 2·diff`, and each value appears at most once, at an earlier index. So for each value we only ask whether those two numbers have already appeared, which a set answers in O(1).

## Approach

1. Create an empty set `seen` and a counter `count = 0`.
2. Scan `nums` from left to right, calling the current number `value`.
3. If both `value - diff` and `value - 2 * diff` are in `seen`, they sit at earlier indices and form a triple ending at `value`, so increase `count`.
4. Add `value` to `seen` and continue.
5. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [0,1,4,6,7,10]`, `diff = 3`. For 0, 1, 4 and 6 at least one of the two needed values is missing (for 6, 3 is absent). For 7, both 4 and 1 are in `seen`, so `count = 1`. For 10, both 7 and 4 are in `seen`, so `count = 2`. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant-time set operations.
- Space: O(n) for `seen`.

## Pitfalls

- The three members need not be neighbours in the array (Example 1 skips the 6 between 4 and 7), so comparing only adjacent elements misses triples.
- Look for `value - 2 * diff`, not `value - diff - 1` or a second copy of `value - diff`.
- No duplicate-triple worry: values are distinct, so each triple is counted once, at its largest value.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | values already scanned (to the left of `value`) |
| `count` | number of arithmetic triples found so far |
| `value` | the current number, treated as the largest of a triple |

narration.2: seen will hold every value to the left of the current one.
narration.3: No triple has been found yet.
narration.5: Treat each number in turn as the last member of a possible triple.
narration.6: The middle and first members must be exactly diff and 2·diff smaller; check both appeared earlier.
narration.7: Both exist, so one more arithmetic triplet ends here.
narration.9: Record this value so later numbers can use it as a first or middle member.
narration.11: Every possible last member has been tried; return the total.
